name: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen
history: A lawyer known as the poor man’s advocate who left the courts to become a Capuchin friar. Sent to preach in the Swiss canton of the Grisons during years of bitter religious and political conflict, he was killed there in 1622. He was the first martyr of the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith.
life: Mark Roy was born at Sigmaringen in Swabia and took a doctorate in law at Freiburg. He spent some years travelling through Europe as tutor to young noblemen, and then practised law at Ensisheim in Alsace, where he took the cases of the poor without fee. Disgusted by the dishonesty of his profession, he entered the Capuchins in 1612, and was given the name Fidelis, from the promise in the Apocalypse: be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life. He served as guardian of several friaries and nursed soldiers through an epidemic. In 1622 the new Congregation de Propaganda Fide sent him to preach in the Prättigau valley, then caught in war between Austrian forces and local Protestant communities. On 24 April, after preaching at Seewis, he was attacked by armed men on the road and killed. He was canonised in 1746.
prayerTo: Saint Fidelis, you defended the poor in the courts and preached Christ in a land divided by war. Pray for lawyers and judges, for missionaries, and for peace between Christians. Help me to be faithful unto death, to speak the truth in love, and to forgive those who oppose me. Amen.
penance: Pray for Christian unity today, and for someone whose beliefs differ from yours. If you can, give to a legal aid charity in honour of the poor man’s lawyer.
meditation: Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life. In what small thing is God asking you to be faithful today?
prayer: God, Who didst vouchsafe to enkindle in blessed Fidelis the fire of thy Seraphim, and to glorify his toil to give men a true knowledge of thee by the palm-branch of martyrdom and by great signs and wonders, be entreated, we beseech thee, for his sake and by his prayers, and so establish us in the knowledge and love of thee, that we also, like him, may be found faithful even unto death in serving of thee. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
